newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee slips on dlr purchase by RBI and SBI.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee slips on dlr purchase by RBI and SBI.

text.p: The Indian rupee slipped against the dollar on Wednesday on aggressive intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and subsequent dollar purchases by the State Bank of India (SBI), dealers said.
Spot rupee opened steady at 35.76/77 on Wednesday, the level at which the RBI had intervened in recent weeks.
RBI intervened early in the day before the rupee could test the 35.75 level, dealers said. RBI hit the market at 35.79 and later at 35.80, buying in lots of $5.0-$10.0 million, they said.
"I guess RBI bought about $200 million today," said a dealer at a foreign bank who was hit by the intervention.
The RBI bought until late afternoon after which dollar demand from the State Bank of India pushed the rupee to the 35.81/82 level, dealers said. The dollar saw a peak of 31.815.
Some dealers said they expected RBI intervention to be eventually replaced by genuine dollar demand from state-run oil and other firms.
The proposed oil price hike, on which the government is expected to take a decision on June 15, may provide the governement an opportunity to correct the overvalued rupee, some dealers said.
This could happen if the government asked oil firms to meet some of their dollar requirements from the market, they said.
One year of stagnant rupee in the face of the dollar's appreciation against other currencies would hurt Indian economy if remedial measures are not taken before long, dealers said.
Forward premiums eased on the prospect of RBI's intervention adding to the comfortable domestic liquidity, dealers said.
The six month annualised forward premium closed steady at 4.42 percent.
